auth.tagline: Meeting protocols, and the recordings behind them.
auth.notLinkedHeading: Your account is not linked yet.
auth.notLinkedBody: Run {command} in Discord, then sign in again. The console finds your recordings by your Discord account, and the link is what connects the two.
auth.guildTagline: Sign-in link for {slug}. It goes to whichever Outline that name is registered against, which need not be the one this deployment uses itself.
auth.guildUnknownNote: If this does not work, either the name is not registered here or its registration is not finished. This page cannot tell those apart, and neither can anybody else — ask whoever sent you the link.
auth.guildUseCentral: Sign in with this deployment’s own Outline instead

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: How this console looks, and which language it speaks. Both belong to this account rather than to a server, and both follow it to another browser.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.note: System follows the operating system, and keeps following it when it turns dark in the evening. Light and dark override it in one direction each.

language.title: Language
language.note: The choice is remembered in a cookie, so the first thing the server sends is already in this language rather than swapping to it after the page has loaded.

security.title: Security
security.note: Neither of these can be switched on yet. They are listed here, and in the account menu, because a plan that is not written down anywhere a person can see is not a plan they can rely on.

consent.title: Consent
consent.intro: What Sturnus may record of you, and in which Discord servers. Consent is given by you, in Discord, with /consent grant — this page is where it can be narrowed or taken back.
consent.serverIdNote: Servers are named here by their Discord id. This console only learns a server's name for the servers this account administers.
consent.emptyNote: Sturnus holds no consent record for you in any server it runs in, so nothing of you is being recorded anywhere. Consent is given in Discord, with /consent grant, and appears here once it exists.

error.signedOut: Your session has ended. Sign in again — nothing about your consent has changed.
error.notDeployed: This console asked the API for your consent records, and the API has no such endpoint yet: it is older than this page. Nothing is listed here rather than an empty list, because an empty list would say you have consented nowhere — and that is a statement about your own data this console cannot currently make.
error.unreachable: The API could not be reached. Nothing is known here about your consent right now, and nothing about it has changed.
error.unknown: Sturnus answered {status} and could not produce your consent records. Nothing has changed.

now.audio: Right now, Sturnus records your voice in this server whenever a session runs. Nothing else of you is captured.
now.audioVideo: Right now, your consent in this server covers your voice and your video.
now.nothing: Nothing of you is being recorded in this server.

granted.noPolicy: Granted {granted}. The policy version it was given under was not recorded.
granted.noDate: It names policy version {policy}. When it was given was not recorded.
granted.neither: Neither the moment it was given nor the policy version it names was recorded.

state.scheduled: It is scheduled to stop on {when}. Until that moment recording continues exactly as it does now; from that moment it does not, within about five seconds.
state.revoked: Withdrawn on {when}. Nothing of you has been recorded in this server since, and nothing will be until consent is granted again with /consent grant in Discord.
state.superseded: This record names policy version {policy}, and this server now runs policy version {current}. A consent naming an older version stops counting, so nothing of you is being recorded here. Granting again happens in Discord, with /consent grant: agreeing to a document is not something this console can do on anybody's behalf.
state.supersededUnknown: This record names a policy version this server has moved past, so it stopped counting and nothing of you is being recorded here. Granting again happens in Discord, with /consent grant.

scope.title: What may be recorded
scope.note: Narrowing takes effect within about five seconds, mid-session if a meeting is running. Widening writes a new consent record naming this server's current policy version.
scope.audioOnly: This server records audio only. It does not offer video consent, so there is no video option here to give or withhold.
scope.videoNotRecordedYet: Sturnus records no video today. Consenting to it records that it would be allowed to; it starts nothing.
scope.locked: The scope of a withdrawn consent cannot be changed. A new one is granted in Discord, with /consent grant.
scope.unchangedDetail: That was already what the record said.
scope.narrowedDetail: It takes effect within about five seconds, mid-session if a meeting is running.
scope.widenedDetail: A new consent record was written, naming this server's current policy version {policy}.
scope.widenedDetailNoPolicy: A new consent record was written. The policy version it names was not reported back.

refusal.videoNotOffered: This server does not offer video consent, so it cannot be consented to here. Nothing changed.
refusal.noConsent: Sturnus holds no consent record for you in this server, so there was nothing to change. Nothing of you is being recorded there.
refusal.alreadyRevoked: This consent has already been withdrawn, so there is nothing left to change. A new one is granted in Discord, with /consent grant.
refusal.noPolicyVersion: This server has no policy version set, so there is no document a consent could name. An administrator sets one before consent can be given or widened.
refusal.unknown: Sturnus refused and did not say why. Nothing changed.

withdraw.title: Withdraw your consent in this server?
withdraw.roleStays: This withdraws the consent record Sturnus stores. It does not remove the Discord consent role from you — the API holds no Discord token, by design, and cannot change anybody's roles. Recording of you still stops within about five seconds, in the middle of a running session if there is one, because the stored record is what is checked on every frame. If the role should go too, it has to be removed in Discord.
withdraw.notDeletion: Withdrawing is not deletion. Every recording that already contains your audio stays exactly where it is. Erasing them is a separate act: /audio delete in Discord.
withdraw.grantAgain: Only you can grant consent again, and only in Discord, with /consent grant. This console cannot do it for you.
withdraw.alreadyScheduled: Recording here is already scheduled to stop on {when}. Withdrawing now asks for it to take effect immediately instead.
withdraw.alreadyDone: Already withdrawn on {when}. There is nothing left to withdraw.
withdraw.doneHeadline: Your consent in this server is withdrawn.
withdraw.doneDetail: It takes effect {when}. Recording of you stops within about five seconds, mid-session if a meeting is running.
withdraw.doneDetailNoInstant: Recording of you stops within about five seconds, mid-session if a meeting is running.
withdraw.heldNone: Sturnus holds no recording containing your audio.
withdraw.heldOne: Sturnus still holds one recording containing your audio. This withdrawal does not delete it; /audio delete in Discord does.
withdraw.heldMany: Sturnus still holds {count} recordings containing your audio. This withdrawal deletes none of them; /audio delete in Discord does.

error.notFoundDetail: The address is wrong, or the page has moved.
error.unreachableDetail: The console reached the browser but could not reach the service behind it. This is not a sign-in problem — signing in again will not help. It usually means the service is restarting, and usually resolves within a minute.
error.genericDetail: The console could not load this page. Trying again is worth one attempt; if it keeps happening, the service is likely unwell rather than the page.

dashboard.intro: Everything Sturnus has recorded of you, across every meeting.
dashboard.failedHeading: Your figures could not be loaded.
dashboard.failedDetail: {reason} Nothing is lost — this page only reads, and the recordings behind it are unaffected.
dashboard.emptyHeading: Sturnus has not recorded you yet.
dashboard.emptyNote: Join a voice channel Sturnus is recording. Once the meeting ends it transcribes what was said, writes the protocol into Outline, and this page fills in: how long you spoke, who you spoke with, and which meetings produced a protocol you were part of.
dashboard.speechNothingMeasured: Your one track was never measured; it predates the measurement. | None of your {count} tracks were measured; they predate the measurement.
dashboard.speechSkipped: One track recorded before Sturnus measured speech is not counted. | {count} tracks recorded before Sturnus measured speech are not counted.
dashboard.protocolsNote: of one session attended | of {count} sessions attended
dashboard.failureSession: Your session is no longer valid.
dashboard.failureNoDashboard: This API has no dashboard yet; it is older than this console.
dashboard.failureUnreachable: The API could not be reached.
dashboard.failureStatus: The API answered {code} and could not produce your figures.

quick.loading: Reading what you can change from here…

consent.title: Your consent
consent.intro: What Sturnus may record of you, and in which servers. This is the same record your settings page holds, and changing it here changes it everywhere.

settings.title: What this server changes often
settings.intro: The handful of settings a server adjusts rather than sets once. Everything else — the policy document, the role ids, the timeouts — is one click away on Bot Settings.
settings.none: Sturnus serves none of these settings for this server. Its whole configuration is on Bot Settings.
settings.withheld: {key} cannot be changed from here: writing it withdraws every consent this server holds, and that warning belongs on Bot Settings rather than in a band on the dashboard.

recordings.intro: These are the meetings you were in. Sturnus records one track per speaker who consented before the recording began, and nobody else — anyone in the channel who did not consent is listed but has no audio here. This is the material each protocol was transcribed from, so when a protocol reads wrong, this is where the answer is.
recordings.failedHeading: Your sessions could not be loaded.
recordings.failedDetail: Nothing was lost; the recordings are on the server either way.
recordings.pastEndHeading: There is nothing on this page.
recordings.pastEndDetail: There is one recording in all, and this page is past the end of it. | There are {count} recordings in all, and this page is past the end of them.
recordings.noMatchHeading: Nothing matched what you asked for.
recordings.noMatchDetail: Your recordings are all still there — this search just does not describe any of them.
recordings.emptyList: No recordings yet. A session appears here once Sturnus has been in a voice channel with you.
recordings.searchPlaceholder: a tag, or words to search for
recordings.searchScopeNote: Tags narrow the list to the recordings labelled that way. The words beside them search what a recording is filed under — its channel, who was in it, whatever else names it. They never search what was said in it: a transcript is everybody else's words, and they consented to a protocol being written from them, not to being searchable.
recordings.missingDetail: Either it never existed, or it belongs to a session you were not in. Sturnus does not say which — the existence of a meeting you were not part of is not something a link should be able to confirm.
recordings.oneFailedHeading: This recording could not be loaded.
recordings.oneFailedDetail: Nothing was lost; the recording is on the server either way.
recordings.noProtocolWritten: No protocol was written for this session.
recordings.alsoInChannelUnrecorded: Also in the channel, without a recording: {people}
recordings.wholeMeetingNote: Every speaker on one transport, which is the only way a conversation makes sense. Solo and mute turn tracks down rather than stopping them, so unmuting lands you where everybody else already is.
recordings.eachTrackNote: For when the question is what one person said rather than what was discussed. Each player here is its own — independent of the transport on the meeting tab, and of every other track.
recordings.noAudio: Nobody in this session had consented before it began, so there is no audio.
recordings.spectrogramShow: Show spectrogram — see where the speech is without listening
recordings.spectrogramFailed: This track could not be drawn. The audio above is unaffected.
recordings.frequencyNote: Frequency runs bottom to top, 0 to {top} kHz. Speech is the banded region low down; a flat picture is a track with nothing on it.
recordings.tagsNote: Labels you put on this recording so you can find it again. Only you can see them — everybody else who was in this meeting has their own, and neither of you sees the other's.
recordings.noTags: This recording has no tags yet.
recordings.addTagLabel: Add a tag to this recording
recordings.tagHint: Separate several with commas. {left} of {max} left on this recording.
recordings.tagTooLong: A tag can be at most {count} characters.
recordings.tagTooMany: A recording can carry at most {count} tags.
recordings.tagAlreadyHeld: That tag is already on this recording.
recordings.tagSaveUnreachable: Your tags could not be saved: the console could not reach the server.
recordings.tagSaveGone: This recording is no longer yours to label.
recordings.tagSaveFailed: Your tags could not be saved. Nothing was changed.
recordings.audioGoneDetail: Sturnus deletes a recording once its retention window closes. Everything written from it stays: the transcript, the protocol, and the measurements taken while it was still here.
recordings.audioGoneNothingToPlay: There is nothing left to play here.
recordings.audioGoneNoTracks: There are no tracks left to play or to draw.
recordings.noDescriptionYet: Nothing has been written about this meeting yet.
recordings.transcriptNote: Assembled the way the protocol was, out of the same words, so the two cannot tell different stories. Each turn carries how far into the meeting it was spoken, on the same clock the transport runs on.
recordings.transcriptRecordingHeading: This meeting is still being recorded.
recordings.transcriptRecordingDetail: Transcription starts when the session closes, so there is nothing to read yet.
recordings.transcriptPendingDetail: One speaker has not been through the transcriber yet. The words appear here once it has finished. | {count} speakers have not been through the transcriber yet. The words appear here once it has finished.
recordings.transcriptSilentHeading: Nothing was said that could be heard.
recordings.transcriptSilentDetail: Every recorded speaker has been through the transcriber, and none of it produced any words.
recordings.transcriptPartial: One speaker is still being transcribed, so this is not all of it yet. | {count} speakers are still being transcribed, so this is not all of it yet.
recordings.transcriptFailedHeading: The words could not be read.
recordings.transcriptFailedDetail: The recording itself is fine — it is only this transcript that did not load.
recordings.nameNote: What this meeting was. Everybody who was in it reads this and any of them can change it — unlike your tags below, which nobody else ever sees.
recordings.nameDescriptionPlaceholder: What was decided, and who is doing what.
recordings.nameReplaceNote: Saving writes both fields at once. A field left empty is cleared for everybody who was in this meeting.
recordings.nameTitleTooLong: A title can be at most {count} characters.
recordings.nameDescriptionTooLong: A description can be at most {count} characters.
recordings.nameSaveUnreachable: This could not be saved: the console could not reach the server.
recordings.nameSaveGone: This recording is no longer yours to name.
recordings.nameSaveRefused: The server refused this text. A title has to fit on one line, and neither field may carry invisible control characters.
recordings.nameSaveFailed: This could not be saved. Nothing was changed.
recordings.protocolsCount: Published to one destination. | Published to {count} destinations.
recordings.protocolsAnnouncedOnlyNote: Sturnus recorded no destination beside this link — either the meeting predates this server naming destinations of its own, or it was published by the single Outline collection named on Bot Settings. There is one link, and nothing else to list.
recordings.protocolsAnnouncedMissing: Sturnus announces one protocol link per meeting in Discord, and none was announced for this one, while the destination below did produce a document. | Sturnus announces one protocol link per meeting in Discord, and none was announced for this one, while the {count} destinations below did produce a document.
recordings.protocolsAnnouncedElsewhere: The link announced in Discord is not one of the destinations below.
recordings.protocolUnknownFormat: As {format}, which is a format this console does not know
recordings.protocolOrphaned: The destination this went to has since been removed. The document is still there and this link still works; nothing new is published here.
recordings.protocolsFailed: Where this meeting was published could not be read. Anything already linked above is unaffected.

calendar.intro: Every day Sturnus recorded a meeting, and what happened on it.
calendar.yearFailedHeading: The calendar for {year} could not be loaded.
calendar.yearFailedDetail: The API answered with an error. Nothing has been lost — this view only reads.
calendar.emptyYearDetail: A cell appears here for every day Sturnus joined a Discord voice channel and recorded a meeting. Invite the bot to a channel and start a session, or {then}
calendar.emptyYearOtherYears: use the arrows above to look at another year.
calendar.emptyYearWait: wait for the first meeting to be recorded.
calendar.dayFailed: The sessions for {date} could not be loaded.
calendar.gridCaption: Recording activity for {year}, one cell per UTC day, laid out as weeks. Use the arrow keys to move between days and Enter to open one.
calendar.daySummary: One session, {duration} in total. | {count} sessions, {duration} in total.
calendar.dayUnknownLengths: One of them has no recorded length. | {count} of them have no recorded length.
calendar.zoneNote: The API groups days in UTC; the clock below is {zone}, so this day runs from {start} to {end} where you are.

reporting.intro: How one Discord server uses Sturnus: how many meetings it has recorded, how long they ran, how many of them were written up, and how that has changed month by month.
reporting.noGuildsHeading: There is nothing here for you yet
reporting.noGuildsBody: This section reports how one Discord server uses Sturnus, and it is open to the administrators of a server where Sturnus is running. You administer none of them right now.
reporting.noGuildsRole: Administrators are the members holding the Discord role that server names in its {setting} setting. Somebody who already has it can grant you that role — Sturnus mirrors the membership from Discord, so the change reaches this console on its own.
reporting.shapeHeading: What a meeting here looks like
reporting.shapeNote: Averages over the meetings that have finished. A figure shown as an em dash is missing rather than zero, and says underneath why there is none.
reporting.tableCaption: Meetings recorded in this server by month, oldest first
reporting.caveatsHeading: Before you quote any of this
reporting.scopeNote: Every figure here is about the server as a whole and never about the people in it. Sturnus sends this page no names and no ids, and there is no per-person breakdown behind it — how long one named person sat in meetings, or spoke in them, is a measure of that person rather than of this server, and that is not something a console should hand out. Counts of people are counts, and stop there.
reporting.emptyHeading: Sturnus has not recorded anything in this server yet
reporting.emptyNote: There are no meetings here to report on, so this page shows no figures rather than a grid of zeros — a zero would be a measurement, and nothing has been measured. Once a meeting happens in a channel Sturnus watches and the people in it have consented, this page fills in: how many meetings, how long they ran, how many of them were written up, and how that changed month by month.
reporting.documentedNothing: Nothing has been recorded in this server yet, so there is nothing to write up.
reporting.documentedAll: The one meeting recorded in this server reached a protocol. | Every one of the {count} meetings recorded in this server reached a protocol.
reporting.documentedPartial: {documented} of the {sessions} meetings recorded in this server reached a protocol — {share} %. The other one was recorded and never written up. | {documented} of the {sessions} meetings recorded in this server reached a protocol — {share} %. The other {count} were recorded and never written up.
reporting.documentedOpen: One meeting is still recording and cannot have been written up yet; it is counted in the total all the same. | {count} meetings are still recording and cannot have been written up yet; they are counted in the total all the same.
reporting.recordedScope: Adds up the length of every meeting in this server that has ended.
reporting.recordedOpenExcluded: The one still recording is not in it — a meeting has no length until it stops. | The {count} still recording are not in it — a meeting has no length until it stops.
reporting.recordedAllEnded: Adds up the length of every meeting this server has recorded, all of which have ended.
reporting.openNone: Nothing is being recorded in this server right now — every meeting it has recorded has ended and has a length.
reporting.openSome: One meeting in this server has no end time yet. | {count} meetings in this server have no end time yet.
reporting.openAmbiguous: That is either a meeting happening at this moment or a session that never closed, and this figure cannot tell the two apart — a session open for days is the second. Neither its length nor its speech is counted anywhere else on this page.
reporting.absentAverageDuration: No meeting in this server has finished, so there is no length to average.
reporting.absentLongestDuration: No meeting in this server has finished, so there is no length to compare.
reporting.absentAverageParticipants: No meeting in this server has finished, so there is no attendance to average.
reporting.absentLargestMeeting: No meeting in this server has finished, so there is no attendance to compare.
reporting.absentNotZero: This is the absence of a figure and not a figure of zero.
reporting.averageDurationNote: The mean length of the meetings that have ended here.
reporting.longestDurationNote: The longest single meeting this server has recorded from start to finish.
reporting.averageParticipantsNote: The mean number of people recorded in a meeting that has ended here.
reporting.largestMeetingNote: The most people recorded in any one meeting in this server.
reporting.participantsNote: How many different people this server has recorded at all. A count and nothing else — Sturnus does not send this page their names, and this page does not ask.
reporting.speechNoTracks: No audio has been recorded in this server, so there is nothing to have measured. The speaking time above is missing rather than zero.
reporting.speechAllMeasured: The one recorded track in this server carries a measured speaking time, so the figure above covers all of what was recorded. | Every one of the {count} recorded tracks in this server carries a measured speaking time, so the figure above covers all of what was recorded.
reporting.speechNoneMeasured: The one recorded track in this server was never measured for speaking time — it predates the columns that hold it — so there is no speaking time here to report. Read the figure above as a measurement that was never taken, not as a server that was quiet. | None of the {count} recorded tracks in this server was ever measured for speaking time — they all predate the columns that hold it — so there is no speaking time here to report. Read the figure above as a measurement that was never taken, not as a server that was quiet.
reporting.speechPartlyMeasured: One of the {tracks} recorded tracks in this server was never measured for speaking time — it predates the columns that hold it — and a sum skips it in silence. | {count} of the {tracks} recorded tracks in this server were never measured for speaking time — they predate the columns that hold it — and a sum skips them in silence.
reporting.speechPartlyMeasuredTotal: The speaking time above is therefore the total for the other one track only: it describes part of what was recorded, and the larger this number grows the further short the figure falls. | The speaking time above is therefore the total for the other {count} tracks only: it describes part of what was recorded, and the larger this number grows the further short the figure falls.
reporting.speechNotQuiet: It does not mean this server was quiet.
reporting.timezoneUnknown: Sturnus did not say which calendar the months below were cut in, so do not assume it is yours: a meeting near midnight falls on either side of a month boundary depending on the zone. Every instant on this page is written in UTC, which may not be that calendar either.
reporting.timezoneKnown: The months below are cut in {zone}, this server's own calendar — not in UTC and not in yours. A meeting that begins at 00:30 belongs to the month the people in it think it does, which is why Sturnus does not bucket by UTC. The instants elsewhere on this page are written in UTC all the same, because a page rendered on a server cannot know your zone, so a meeting near a month boundary can carry a UTC date that reads as the neighbouring month.
reporting.spanNothing: No meeting has been recorded in this server yet, so this report covers no time at all.
reporting.spanBetween: Everything recorded in this server between {from} and {to}.
reporting.spanPartial: Everything recorded in this server. Only one end of the span is known: {at}.
reporting.spanUnreadable: Everything recorded in this server. Sturnus dated the span with something this console could not read as a time, so neither end of it can be shown.
reporting.monthsNothing: No month in this server has any recording in it yet.
reporting.monthsTooLong: Only the months in which something was recorded are listed, oldest first. This server's history spans more than {years} years, which is too long to list month by month, so the quiet months between these are not shown as rows — two rows next to each other are not necessarily neighbouring months.
reporting.monthsOldestFirst: Every month from the first recording in this server to the most recent one, oldest first.
reporting.monthsAllBusy: Something was recorded in each of them.
reporting.monthsSomeSilent: The one month in which nothing was recorded is listed with a zero rather than left out, so a quiet stretch reads as a gap instead of closing up. | The {count} months in which nothing was recorded are listed with a zero rather than left out, so a quiet stretch reads as a gap instead of closing up.
reporting.monthSilent: {month}: nothing was recorded in this server.
reporting.monthDetail: {month}: one meeting, {recorded} recorded, {documented} written up. | {month}: {count} meetings, {recorded} recorded, {documented} written up.
reporting.monthDetailUnmeasured: {month}: one meeting, no length recorded, {documented} written up. | {month}: {count} meetings, no length recorded, {documented} written up.
reporting.errorSession: Your session has ended. Sign in again to see this server's figures.
reporting.errorNotAdmin: You do not administer this server. Administrators are the members holding the role named by that guild's `admin_role_id`.
reporting.errorUnknownGuild: Sturnus does not know this server, or you no longer administer it — it answers the same way to both. Reload the page; the list of servers is rebuilt from Discord.
reporting.errorUnreachable: Could not reach the API. Nothing here is out of date on purpose; check the connection and retry.
reporting.errorStatus: Sturnus answered {status} and could not produce this server's figures. Nothing is known about why.

roster.total: {count} person has a consent record in this server. | {count} people have a consent record in this server.
roster.inForce: {count} of the {shown} on this page is in force right now. | {count} of the {shown} on this page are in force right now.
roster.beyondEnd: This page of the roster does not exist any more — the list has changed since this link was made. Nobody is missing; everybody is on an earlier page.
roster.fromDirectory: Name taken from this server's Discord directory; the consent record itself carries none.
roster.unresolved: No name anywhere: the consent record carries none, and this server's Discord directory has no entry for this id — so this row shows the bare Discord user id. Consent is given by a Discord command, and a name is only learned when somebody turns up in a session that was recorded.
roster.unlisted: No name on the consent record, and this server's Discord directory could not be read just now — so this row shows the bare Discord user id.

effective.nowNote: Now, unless another moment is chosen here. Withdrawing without opening this behaves exactly as it always has.
effective.help: A moment in the past is a statement about recordings that already exist. A moment in the future is a scheduled withdrawal: recording continues until then, and stops within about five seconds of it.
effective.unreadable: That is not a moment this console can read. Pick a date and a time, or go back to now.
effective.beforeGrant: This consent was granted {granted}. A withdrawal cannot take effect before the consent it withdraws — pick that moment or a later one.
effective.pastNone: This takes effect {when}, which is in the past. Sturnus holds no recording containing their audio, so nothing falls inside it.
effective.pastOne: This takes effect {when}, which is in the past. Sturnus holds {count} recording containing their audio; it falls inside the withdrawal if it is dated on or after that moment.
effective.pastMany: This takes effect {when}, which is in the past. Sturnus holds {count} recordings containing their audio; whichever of them are dated on or after that moment fall inside the withdrawal.
effective.notDeletion: None of them are deleted by this. A withdrawal governs what may be recorded, never what already was — erasing a recording is a separate act, /audio purge in Discord.
effective.futureNote: This is a scheduled withdrawal rather than an immediate one. Recording continues exactly as it does now until {when}, and stops within about five seconds of it.
effective.fromNone: No recording containing their audio falls on or after {when}.
effective.fromOne: {count} recording containing their audio falls on or after {when}. It was not deleted.
effective.fromMany: {count} recordings containing their audio fall on or after {when}. None of them were deleted.

bulk.title: Withdraw consent for {count} person? | Withdraw consent for {count} people?
bulk.lead: It applies to this person and to nobody else: | It applies to these people and to nobody else:
bulk.roleStays: This withdraws the consent records Sturnus stores. It removes the Discord consent role from nobody — the API holds no Discord token, by design, and cannot change anybody's roles. Recording of each of them still stops within about five seconds, in the middle of a running session if there is one, because the stored record is what is checked on every frame. If the roles should go too, remove them in Discord.
bulk.recordingsKept: Nothing already recorded is deleted. Every recording that already contains any of their audio stays exactly where it is; erasing one is a separate act — /audio purge in Discord.
bulk.audit: This is written to the audit log, one line per person: your Discord account, whose consent you withdrew, and when.
bulk.none: Nothing is selected, so there is nothing to withdraw.
bulk.tooMany: Sturnus withdraws at most {max} consents in one request, and {count} are selected. That bound is one page of this roster, so clear part of the selection and work through it a page at a time.
bulk.effectiveLegend: Effective from, for everybody named above
bulk.effectiveNote: Now, unless another moment is chosen here. The same moment applies to every person in this withdrawal.
bulk.tally: {count} of the {requested} named was withdrawn. | {count} of the {requested} named were withdrawn.
bulk.perPerson: What happened to each of them:
bulk.outcomeAlready: Already withdrawn — by somebody else, or in another tab. Nothing changed just now, and nothing needed to.
bulk.outcomeNoRecord: Sturnus holds no consent record for this person at all, so there was nothing to withdraw. They are not being recorded.
bulk.outcomeBeforeGrant: Refused: the moment chosen falls before this person's consent was granted, and a withdrawal cannot take effect before the consent it withdraws.
bulk.outcomeRefused: Refused, and Sturnus did not say why. Nothing of theirs was changed.

list.queuedHeading: The order this server’s work will run in
list.queuedNote: Every session with a job still queued or running, first to last. This is the order a worker reaches them in, and it is the order the controls here change.
list.queuedNone: Nothing is queued or running in this server, so there is no order to set.
list.queuedSome: One session is waiting to run. | {count} sessions are waiting to run, in the order shown.
list.unqueuedHeading: Listed, but not in the queue
list.unqueuedNote: These sessions have no job queued or running, so there is nothing about them to reorder and no handle to move them by. Each one is here because it is being recorded at this moment, or because nothing will move it on without a person.
list.unqueuedNone: Every unfinished session in this server has work queued for it.
list.unqueuedWaiting: One session is listed with nothing queued, and it is not waiting on a person. | {count} sessions are listed with nothing queued, and none of them is waiting on a person.
list.unqueuedStuck: One session here needs somebody: nothing queued will move it on. | {count} of the {total} sessions here need somebody: nothing queued will move them on.
list.pagerWaiting: Pages of the sessions with nothing queued

order.instructions: Press Enter or Space to pick a session up, then Up and Down to move it, Home to send it to the front and End to the back. Enter puts it down where it is; Escape leaves it where it was. It can also be dragged with a mouse, within the page it is on.
order.pickedUp: {session} picked up, position {position} of {total}. Move it with the arrow keys, then press Enter to put it down.
order.droppedBack: {session} was put back where it was, and nothing was changed.
order.moved: Moved. One session’s place in this queue changed. | Moved. {count} sessions changed place — going first is expressed as everything that was ahead going second, so rows nobody touched carry new numbers too.
order.unchanged: Nothing to do: this queue was already in that order.
order.stale: Somebody else moved something in this queue while that was in the air, so nothing was written. The list below is the order as it now stands — move it again if it still needs moving.
order.failedSignedOut: Your session has ended, so nothing was moved. Sign in again.
order.failedGone: The session has left this queue, or you no longer administer this server — Sturnus answers the same way to both. Nothing was written; refresh to see where things stand.
order.failedRefused: Sturnus refused that as malformed and wrote nothing. That is a fault in this console rather than anything to do differently, so reloading the page is the only thing worth trying.
order.failedUnreachable: Could not reach the API, so nothing was moved. The order below is the last one read.
order.failedUnknown: Sturnus could not move it and said nothing about why. Nothing was written.

rules.heading: Change the whole order at once
rules.note: Two ways to re-rank everything this server has outstanding. Each rewrites every priority in the queue, so each says what it will do before it does it.
rules.wholeServer: This reaches every session this server has outstanding, including any the list above was cut short of showing.
rules.neverForward: Nothing is moved forward. A session going first is expressed as everything that was ahead of it going second, so this holds work back rather than speeding anything up — and it holds it back behind every other server’s work as well, not only behind this server’s.
rules.notUndone: Pressing the other button afterwards does not undo this. It writes an order of its own on top of the numbers this one leaves behind.

participants.name: Biggest meetings first
participants.blurb: Ranks by how many people were recorded in each session.
participants.ties: Sessions with the same number of participants keep the order they already had.

short.name: Shortest recordings first
short.blurb: Ranks by how much audio has been measured, and a session nothing has measured ranks last.
short.unmeasured: A recording nothing has ever measured has no length to rank by, so it goes after every measured one and keeps the place it had. Most sessions are unmeasured until they have been transcribed once, so on a queue of fresh recordings this changes very little — it earns its place on a queue of re-queued ones.

settings.kindUnresolved: Configured, but not in the copy
settings.mirrorSynced: These names come from the copy Sturnus made of this server at {moment}.
settings.mirrorSyncedAgo: These names come from the copy Sturnus made of this server at {moment}, {age} ago.
settings.mirrorStale: These names come from the copy Sturnus made of this server at {moment} — {age} ago. Anything renamed or deleted in Discord since then is not shown here.
settings.mirrorNeverSwept: Sturnus has not copied this server from Discord yet, so there is nothing to choose from. Enter the id by hand, or wait for the bot's next sweep.
settings.mirrorSyncUnreadable: Sturnus reported a time for its last sweep that this console cannot read, so how current these names are is not known.
settings.mirrorEmpty: Sturnus has a copy of this server and found nothing in it for this key, so this key still asks for an id.
settings.directoryUnavailable: The channel and role names could not be read, so this key asks for an id, as it always did. Everything else on this page works as it always did too.
settings.collectionsUnavailable: The Outline collections could not be read, so this key asks for a collection id, as it always did.
settings.unresolvedChannel: One of the ids above matches no channel in the copy. It may have been deleted in Discord, or the copy may not have caught up — either way it is still what Sturnus is configured with.
settings.unresolvedRole: This id matches no role in the copy. It may have been deleted in Discord, or the copy may not have caught up — either way it is still what Sturnus is configured with.
settings.unresolvedCollection: This id matches no collection in the copy. It may have been deleted in Outline, or the copy may not have caught up — either way it is still what Sturnus is configured with.
settings.manualNote: Stored exactly as typed. The list only knows what the last copy found.
settings.noChannelsChosen: No channel chosen. Sturnus records nothing in this server until at least one is.
settings.groupTabs: Settings, grouped by what they are for
settings.groupOtherNote: These keys are in none of the groups above: they reached the API after those groups were written, and this page would rather show a key it cannot file than quietly leave it out. Nothing else about them is different — each is set, cleared and takes effect exactly as every other key here does.

destinations.title: Destinations
destinations.intro: Where this server publishes its protocols. A meeting can go to several destinations in several formats; each is written on its own, so one destination being unreachable does not lose the others.
destinations.noGuildsHeading: There is nothing here for you yet
destinations.noGuildsBody: This page says where one Discord server publishes its protocols, and it is open to the administrators of a server where Sturnus is running. You administer none of them right now.
destinations.noGuildsRole: Administrators are the members holding the Discord role that server names in its {setting} setting. Somebody who already has it can grant you that role — Sturnus mirrors the membership from Discord, so the change reaches this console on its own.
destinations.loadFailed: This server’s destinations could not be read.
destinations.serversFailed: The servers you administer could not be read, so there is nothing to configure yet.
destinations.emptyHeading: This server has no destination of its own
destinations.emptyNote: Nothing here is broken. A destination is something somebody adds, and until one is added this server keeps publishing where Bot Settings says.
destinations.nameHint: What this destination is called here. It is published nowhere; it is what tells two destinations apart on this page.
destinations.nameLockedNote: A name cannot be changed here. Sturnus addresses a stored destination by its name, so renaming one means adding a destination and removing this one — which is what the two actions below are for.
destinations.formatHint: What is written and what carries it away. A format decides both: an Outline document and a Markdown file are not the same text with a different extension.
destinations.formatOutlineNote: Created in a collection in Outline
destinations.formatMarkdownNote: Stored by Sturnus, read through this console
destinations.formatHtmlNote: Stored by Sturnus, read through this console
destinations.formatUnknownDetail: Configured here, and not a format this console knows
destinations.formatsNote: These are the formats this deployment publishes. PDF and Confluence are specified and not built, so they are not offered here rather than offered and then refused — a choice that a save rejects teaches people not to trust the choices beside it.
destinations.collectionHint: The collection each protocol is created in. The same list Bot Settings offers for its own document_target.
destinations.collectionsUnavailable: The Outline collections could not be read, so this asks for a collection id.
destinations.collectionManual: Enter a collection id by hand
destinations.unresolvedCollection: This id matches no collection in the copy Sturnus made of Outline. It may have been deleted there, or the copy may not have caught up — either way it is still what this destination is configured with.
destinations.prefixHint: Where in Sturnus’s own store the file is written. Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore, and / between them; the meeting and the destination are appended.
destinations.enabledHint: Switching a destination off is not forgetting how it was configured. It stays here, and nothing is published to it.
destinations.rowUnknownFormat: {format}, into {target} — a format this console does not know. Whether it can be published is this deployment’s own answer.
destinations.primaryNote: Enabled destinations are written oldest first, and the link Sturnus posts in Discord is the first one’s. It does not move when a destination is renamed.
destinations.deleteConfirmBody: Nothing already published is deleted. Every protocol written here stays where it is and its link keeps working; Sturnus stops publishing to it and nothing else.
destinations.secretStored: A credential is stored for this destination.
destinations.secretNeverShown: Sturnus never shows a stored credential, here or anywhere: no route returns one. Replacing it and clearing it are the only two things that can be done to it, and each has a button of its own — an empty box rendered beside a stored credential is how one gets wiped by somebody correcting a typo in a name.
destinations.secretUnused: None of the formats above reads a stored credential yet: Outline is published with this deployment’s own Outline token, and the two file formats are written into this deployment’s own store. One set here is kept for the destinations that will read it.
destinations.secretClearConfirmBody: It cannot be recovered afterwards — Sturnus holds no copy that anything can read back. Publishing to this destination carries on with no credential until another is stored.
destinations.nameTaken: This server already has a destination with that name.
destinations.targetEmpty: A destination needs somewhere to write to.
destinations.targetNotCollection: An Outline collection id: no spaces in it, and no slash at the front.
destinations.targetNotPrefix: Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore, separated by / — no slash at the front, none at the end, and no “..”.
destinations.errorRefused: Sturnus refused that destination. This console offers the formats it believes this deployment builds, so a refusal here means the deployment’s own list differs from it.
destinations.errorSession: Your session has ended. Sign in again, then retry — nothing was written.
destinations.errorGone: Sturnus no longer knows this server or this destination, or you no longer administer it — it answers the same way to all three. Reload the page.
destinations.errorDuplicate: This server already has a destination with that name.
destinations.errorUnreachable: Could not reach the API. Nothing was written; check the connection and retry.
destinations.errorStatus: Sturnus answered {status} and did not say why. What was written, if anything, is not known.
destinations.fallbackInUse: No destination here is switched on, so this server still publishes where document_target on Bot Settings points: one Outline document per meeting. Switching one on here takes over from that setting completely.
destinations.fallbackReplaced: This server publishes to the one destination above, and document_target on Bot Settings is no longer used for it — the destinations here replace that setting rather than adding to it. | This server publishes to the {count} destinations above, and document_target on Bot Settings is no longer used for them — the destinations here replace that setting rather than adding to it.

signInLink.title: Sign-in link
signInLink.intro: A server can sign its people in against its own Outline rather than the one this deployment is configured with, through a link its administrators hand out themselves.
signInLink.optional: None of this is required. A server that configures nothing here goes on signing in exactly as it does today, through this deployment’s own Outline.
signInLink.serversFailed: The servers administered by this account could not be read, so there is nothing to configure yet.
signInLink.noGuildsHeading: There is nothing here for you yet
signInLink.noGuildsBody: This page gives one Discord server a sign-in link of its own, and it is open to the administrators of a server where Sturnus is running. This account administers none of them right now.
signInLink.noGuildsRole: Administrators are the members holding the Discord role that server names in its {setting} setting. Somebody who already has it can grant you that role — Sturnus mirrors the membership from Discord, so the change reaches this console on its own.
signInLink.loadFailed: This server’s sign-in configuration could not be read.
signInLink.stateAbsentHeading: This server has no sign-in link
signInLink.stateAbsentDetail: Its members sign in through this deployment’s own Outline, which is the ordinary arrangement and needs nothing from this page.
signInLink.stateIncompleteHeading: This link does not work yet
signInLink.stateIncompleteDetail: The client is registered but its secret has not been supplied, so the link answers exactly as a name nobody has registered — the same reply, deliberately, so that a stranger walking a list of names cannot tell a half-configured server from one that is not here at all. Store the client secret below and the link starts working.
signInLink.stateLiveDetail: Anybody who follows it signs in through this server’s own Outline. Sturnus never publishes it anywhere — {slug} is only reachable by somebody who was given it.
signInLink.linkHint: Distribute this yourself. There is no page anywhere that lists the servers Sturnus serves, and that absence is what keeps this deployment from disclosing which organisations use it.
signInLink.registrationNone: Nothing is registered for this server. Register an OAuth application in its own Outline first, pointing its redirect URI at this deployment’s console callback, then enter its details here.
signInLink.removeConfirmBody: The link stops working at once and its name is released, so another server may claim it afterwards. The stored client secret goes with it. Nobody signed in loses their session, and this server’s members can still sign in through this deployment’s own Outline.
signInLink.slugHint: 3 to 32 characters: lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, beginning with a letter. Beginning with a letter is what keeps a sign-in name and a Discord server id from being confusable in a link somebody reads.
signInLink.slugPermanenceNew: It becomes part of a public address, so choose a word this server is content to be known by. Nothing is corrected for you: a capital letter is refused rather than lowercased, because a name quietly rewritten on the way in is a name nobody recognises in the link they handed out.
signInLink.slugPermanenceChange: Changing it changes the link. Anything already handed out stops working immediately, and the old name is released for another server to claim.
signInLink.slugEmpty: A sign-in name is needed — it is the word that appears in the link.
signInLink.slugLength: A sign-in name is between {min} and {max} characters long.
signInLink.slugShape: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens only, beginning with a letter. No spaces, no capitals, and no hyphen at either end.
signInLink.baseUrlHint: Where this server’s own Outline lives — for example https://outline.acme.example. A path is fine; a query string or a fragment is not, because Sturnus builds its own.
signInLink.baseUrlEmpty: The address of this server’s Outline is needed.
signInLink.urlShape: An https address, with no username, no query string and no fragment. Plain http is refused because the authorisation code travels over this, and a username in front of the host is refused because it makes the address read as one host and reach another.
signInLink.clientIdHint: From the OAuth application registered in that Outline. It is the half of the pair that is not a secret, so it is shown here and is safe to read back.
signInLink.clientIdEmpty: The client id of that OAuth application is needed.
signInLink.clientIdLong: That is longer than a client id can be. Check that a secret has not been pasted into this field by mistake.
signInLink.redirectOwnLabel: This server uses a callback address of its own
signInLink.redirectDefaultHint: Leave this as it is unless there is a reason not to: the OAuth application returns to this deployment’s own console callback, which is what nearly every server wants.
signInLink.redirectOwnHint: The address the OAuth application returns to after somebody authorises. It must match what is registered in that Outline exactly.
signInLink.redirectEmpty: A callback address is needed, or untick the box above to use this deployment’s own.
signInLink.providerHint: Outline is the only provider this deployment can complete a sign-in against, so there is nothing to choose. A registration against anything else would be a link that is permanently and silently broken.
signInLink.providerUnsupported: This registration names {provider}, which this deployment cannot exchange a sign-in with. Saving it would leave the link broken with nothing to show for it.
signInLink.secretStored: A client secret is stored for this server.
signInLink.secretNone: No client secret is stored, so the link does not work yet.
signInLink.secretNeverShown: Sturnus shows a stored client secret nowhere, this page included: it is encrypted against this server and this purpose, and no route returns it. Replacing and clearing are the only things that can be done with it, and each has its own button — an empty box beside a stored secret is how one disappears while somebody is correcting a typo elsewhere.
signInLink.secretRotationNote: It is also worth re-entering after a master-key rotation. A secret wrapped by a key this deployment no longer holds makes the link stop working silently from the outside, and typing it again is what re-wraps it.
signInLink.secretClearConfirmBody: It cannot be recovered afterwards — Sturnus keeps no copy anything could read back. The link stops working at once and starts answering exactly as an unregistered name, while the registration and its name stay yours. That is what to do when a secret has leaked.
signInLink.savedRegistered: The client is registered. The link starts working once its secret is stored.
signInLink.savedRemoved: The registration was removed and its name released.
signInLink.savedSecretSet: The client secret was stored. The link works from now on.
signInLink.savedSecretCleared: The client secret was cleared. The link answers as an unregistered name until a new one is stored.
signInLink.scopeNote: This governs signing in to the console, and nothing else. Linking a Discord account with {command} always runs against this deployment’s own client, permanently: the process that serves it does not hold the master key and therefore cannot unwrap a server’s secret — which is what keeps the internet-facing half of Sturnus unable to decrypt anything at all.
signInLink.errorRefused: Sturnus refused this registration. Every field this console checks had already passed, so its idea of a valid registration and this deployment’s no longer agree.
signInLink.errorSession: The session has expired. Sign in again and retry — nothing was written.
signInLink.errorGone: Sturnus no longer knows this server, or this account no longer administers it, or there is nothing registered for it — the reply is the same for all three, on purpose. Reload the page.
signInLink.errorNameTaken: That sign-in name is not available. Sturnus does not say whether it is held elsewhere or reserved for itself, and will not — choose a different one.
signInLink.errorUnreachable: The API could not be reached. Nothing was written; check the connection and retry.
signInLink.errorStatus: Sturnus answered {status} and gave no reason. What was written, if anything, is unknown.

select.empty: There is nothing to choose from.

datePicker.unreadable: That is not a date that exists.

chipInput.placeholder: Add a tag, or just type
chipInput.chipsAndText: {count} tag, and searching for “{text}”. | {count} tags, and searching for “{text}”.

list.empty: There is nothing in this list.
list.selectedWithOffPage: {count} row selected, {away} of them not on this page. | {count} rows selected, {away} of them not on this page.
list.bulkScope: “{action}” would apply to {count} row. | “{action}” would apply to {count} rows.

gallery.title: Console controls
gallery.intro: Every control in app/components/ui, in the states a reviewer has to see: empty, filled, disabled, refused, and a list too long to scroll. This page exists so that the controls can be read without running the rest of the console, and it is reachable in development only.
gallery.list: List that opens, with bulk actions
gallery.stateDay: As a day, with no time
gallery.panelOverview: This panel was built when the page opened, because its tab was the one the address named.
gallery.panelQueue: This panel did not exist until its tab was pressed. That is the whole of the lazy mounting: a panel whose data is expensive must not load because it exists.
gallery.panelConsents: And this one is still not built until somebody asks for it.
gallery.rowAction: The actions a row reveals live here, and belong to whichever page is using the list.
